participants: Adam (Primal Instinct, setter — appears in the transcript as 'Speaker 2', addressed by name at 00:00:00)
summary: A ten-minute debrief between a closer and his setter immediately after a call that did not convert. Richard gave feedback on one specific set — a prospect ('Brent') who was qualified on goal and price tolerance but wanted to keep his existing training and only add a couple of kettlebell sessions a week, whom Richard says should have been routed to 'Primal University' rather than to a one-to-one closing call. Adam said he did not know he could route leads there and did not have the link. They then worked through the day's pipeline: an Orlando prospect who no-showed citing a back injury, and two others rescheduling, one for a family emergency. Richard disclosed his show rate for the day, encouraged Adam to keep sending volume regardless of quality, and told him to raise the routing question with Chris at the team meeting later that day.
notable: Show rate disclosed directly: 'I began with, I don't know, eight calls on my calendar. Only one showed so far and that was the [Brent].' One in eight on the day. Since only shows are recorded, any close rate computed from this corpus is measured against a denominator that excludes roughly seven-eighths of booked calls.

A second product tier exists that does not appear anywhere in the stated offer: 'Primal University'. It is used as an explicit downsell for prospects who will not buy the one-to-one — 'if someone is like, hey, I just want to sort of try it out, I would push them a little bit more towards it' — and Richard confirms he ran it on this call: 'with him I did down sell him, like I gave him an idea from what Primal University looks like'. No price for it is stated anywhere in the call.

Routing to that tier is informal and undocumented. The setter did not know it existed as an option — 'I just don't have the link for the primary university thing... I didn't know that I could send people there as well that didn't want it. I was just booking the calendar' — and Richard's guidance was to ask a manager rather than cite a policy: 'you have a team meeting in like one and half hours... I would say also ask Chris about that, what he would think. I think Kim does the same thing.'

The setter described the lead source itself as low-intent and being actively repaired upstream: 'there's a lot of volume for sure, but there's literally low intent... these leads are kind of like cold. Like they didn't directly ask for the help. So they're kind of fixing that right now from the upstream part, from the ads and everything.'

Richard stated he wants unqualified prospects booked anyway so he can use live calls as practice: 'I want to take as many life calls as possible so if you send someone like that to me I'd rather just take it as a role play call.'

Both men treated a prospect's stated back injury as a lie before landing on a semantic distinction. Adam: 'I don't know what the [f---] you mean by he broke his back. I think that's just [cap].' Richard: 'It's definitely that broke his back. That's Cap... he told me like, no, I'm sorry, I hurt my back. That's not broke. That's the difference.' Richard then declined to push the rebook: 'if he hurt his back... it's kind of not on the show anymore.'

Same pattern applied to a family emergency: 'I don't know why people do, I have family issues, like they just put their family inside of the garbage can' and 'some people may just make excuses for everything and I hate it. Like, just tell me, I don't want to take the call.'

Adam described telling a prospect to be transparent about not wanting the call; Richard advised against it on retention grounds: 'if you do that, then he's not going to show anyone. Then you've definitely lost him.'

Ability to pay was inferred from nationality: 'If the Orlando guy showed, he would have been an instant close. Just based on his data. Yeah, it's an American guy. I feel like he would have the money.'

Staff named: Chris (runs the team meeting, escalation point for routing questions) and Kim (referenced as already routing low-intent prospects to Primal University — consistent with KFS, Kim Forbes-Sobers, in the setter code list).

Prospect first names surfaced and partially garbled by transcription: Brent (the debriefed call), an unnamed 'Orlando guy', 'Ray' and 'Rach'. None are recorded as prospects here; no sales record is written from this file.
